Definition: from G4012 and G991; to look all around:--look (round) about (on).
BiblicalUsage: Periblepo means to look round about. Jesus looked round about on the Pharisees with anger, grieved for the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch forth thine hand” — and the hand was restored. Luke tells it again: looking round about upon them all, He healed the man with the withered hand.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the look round about is the look of a Lord who sees hardness and heals anyway: His anger is at the heart, and His mercy is for the hand.
